properties.name: The CLI describes any served tool in full — its input schema with types and required fields, and the lessons tools/list carries for it
properties.statement:
Step 4 of the plan to make the `--call` door work for an agent that cannot use MCP (Anthony, 2026-10-01; his idea 5 in using_call.md).

Today find_tools gives parameter NAMES only (query.rs ~853). The lessons a DesignRule or TemporalFact hangs on a tool ride only its tools/list description (lessons.rs:230), which a door agent never reads. So it learns types from refusals, one round trip per mistake, and never meets the lessons.

MUST:
- `--describe <tool>` prints the tool's full input schema and its description including the appended lessons, exactly as tools/list serves them.
- A whole-list form lets an instructions generator render a reference from the binary.
- What it prints is the served list itself, so it cannot disagree with what an MCP session is offered.
